key_insight: This paper shows that histopathology images can be used to infer transcriptomic signals, then combine those inferred molecular features with clinical data to better predict breast cancer response to neoadjuvant therapy. The key breakthrough is a two-stage AI pipeline that reduces dependence on scarce labeled treatment-response data.
problem_solved: Deep learning biomarkers in oncology often fail to scale because labeled outcome data are limited. This work addresses how to predict pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer when direct training labels are scarce.
method: Stage 1: Train a model on 8,742 patients across 32 cancer types to infer transcriptome information directly from histopathology images.
Validate the inferred molecular signals with pathologist review and spatial agreement against measured gene expression.
Stage 2: Use the inferred transcriptome features plus clinical variables to predict pCR in breast cancer biopsies.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical blueprint for leveraging weakly labeled or label-scarce biomedical data through multi-stage representation learning. It suggests that learning biologically meaningful intermediate features can improve downstream prediction while making models more interpretable and scalable.

paper_title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies
paper_authors: Jungkyu Park, Dhruva Biswas, Joseph Cappadona, Cerise Tang, Ken G. Zeng
